1. [Quadratic probe sequence] The response states the quadratic probing sequence as p_i = (h(k) + i^2) mod m for i = 0, 1, 2, ... with arithmetic modulo the prime table size m. (importance 3/5)
2. [First half probes distinct] The response examines the first floor(m/2)+1 quadratic probing steps for a table of prime size that is at least half empty, indexing i from 0 to floor(m/2), and states that these are pairwise distinct to prove we can always insert. (importance 5/5)
3. [Tight i+j bound] The response bounds i + j ≤ 2*floor(m/2) − 1 < m for the quadratic probing table of prime size, using the constraint i < j to tighten the bound, so m does not divide (i + j), proving we can always insert when at least half empty. (importance 5/5)
4. [Primality necessity] The response notes that the primality assumption is essential because composite table sizes can produce collisions among the first floor(m/2)+1 probes. (importance 2/5)
5. [Pigeonhole argument] The response explicitly applies a counting or pigeonhole argument: floor(m/2)+1 distinct probe locations versus at most floor(m/2) occupied slots guarantees at least one probed slot is empty. (importance 4/5)
6. [Insertion conclusion] The response concludes that a new element can always be inserted into the hash table within the first floor(m/2)+1 probes when m is prime and the table is at least half empty. (importance 4/5)
7. [General hash value] The response states or demonstrates that the proof holds for any initial hash value h(k), not just favorable ones, when the table is at least half empty. (importance 2/5)
8. [Interrobang used] The response includes the interrobang (?!) at least once. (importance 3/5)
9. [Semicolons used] The response includes at least one semicolon as a standard punctuation mark. (importance 2/5)
10. [Periods used] The response includes at least one period as a standard punctuation mark, as the question requires every standard mark at least once. (importance 1/5)
11. [Question marks used] The response includes at least one question mark as a standard punctuation mark, distinct from the interrobang. (importance 1/5)
12. [Avoids overclaiming] Avoids claiming that all m quadratic probes are pairwise distinct; the response restricts the distinctness claim to the first floor(m/2)+1 probes when the table is at least half empty. (importance 2/5)

3. [Concentration from calibration] The concentration is computed as x = (0.8 − 0.1306) / 51721 ≈ 1.29×10⁻⁵ mol/L, subtracting the 0.1306 intercept before dividing by the 51721 slope. (importance 3/5)
4. [Actual moles from 10 mL] The actual moles of hydrazine are computed as concentration × 0.010 L ≈ 1.29×10⁻⁷ mol using the total 10 mL experiment volume, avoiding any extra dilution factor for the 5 mL electrolyte aliquot. (importance 3/5)
